QF.id: Cat III AIF Due Diligence and Risk_17

question.text: During a market stress scenario, Cat III AIF strategies may face:

answer.text: Liquidity constraints, margin/capital-call pressure, counterparty default risk, illiquid positions, and difficulty closing positions at optimal value

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes how Cat III AIF strategies are exposed to illiquidity in market stress, with positions becoming illiquid in disrupted markets and managers facing difficulty exiting at optimal value. Derivative and leveraged positions add margin and capital-call pressure, and counterparty default risk rises when stress spreads across financial intermediaries. Taken together, these are the source-backed stress impacts a Cat III AIF must plan for. The Trap: "Guaranteed gains" and "no impact" contradict the workbook's stress narrative, and "interest rate boost" is an unrelated macro outcome rather than a stress impact on the AIF itself. Note: Stress-period liquidity, counterparty, and derivative-margin risks are discussed in the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
